description: Pedestrian Counting System - Sensor Locations is a dataset listed in Australian national open data portal, an open data portal, published or maintained by City of Melbourne Open Data. This dataset contains status, location and directional information for each pedestrian sensor device installed throughout the city. The sensorid column can be used to merge the data with related datasets. Since the inauguration of the Pedestrian Counting System in 2009, some sensor devices have been removed or relocated. Coverage: City of Melbourne Open Data. The portal files it under the publisher City of Melbourne Open Data. Its tags are cityreactivation, directions, foot-traffic, locations, pedestrian. It offers 5 resource(s) in CSV, GEOJSON, JSON, SHP. The portal shows 2026-09-29 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-3.0-AU. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support cycling and walking network and demand studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ckan-au-portal.
